context:
Single-line change in benchbox/core/platform_registry.py:
  line 212: "driver_package": None  →  "driver_package": "polars"

The PyPI package name is "polars" (confirmed: importlib.metadata.version("polars") works).
No other files need changes - the announcement line in commands/run.py already handles
driver_version_actual from database_config.

For the unit test, follow the pattern in tests/unit/cli/test_run_driver_version_announcement.py.
Specifically, add a test where the mock DatabaseConfig has driver_version_actual="1.36.1"
and platform="polars", and assert that the console output contains "[driver 1.36.1]".
description:
The Polars platform entry in platform_registry.py has driver_package=None (line 212),
which causes ensure_driver_version() to skip version detection entirely. As a result,
the "Running ..." announcement line for polars runs never shows a driver version:

  Running tpch on polars at scale 0.1          ← no [driver X.Y.Z] clause

The fix is a one-line change: set driver_package="polars" in the platform registry.
After that change, ensure_driver_version() will detect the installed polars version
via importlib.metadata and populate database_config.driver_version_actual, which
the announcement line already uses.

Context: clickhouse-connect (line 306) and psycopg2-binary (line 485) already have
driver_package set correctly and already display their versions. This item closes
the remaining gap for the polars platform.

Note: polars runs in DataFrame mode (supports_sql=False, default_mode=dataframe).
The driver_package field is used purely for version detection - it is independent
of the execution mode.

anti_patterns.why: driver_package is only used by ensure_driver_version() for version detection, not execution routing
sqlite3 is a stdlib module with no PyPI package

preserves.behavior: All existing fast unit tests pass after the change
SQLite platform keeps driver_package=None (line 200) - sqlite3 is stdlib, has no importlib.metadata entry
polars DataFrame execution path continues to work correctly (driver_package is only for version detection)
